evals.prompt: Protocol or ABC for our payment provider interface? Someone on the team says Protocols can't share code and isinstance on them is way too slow.
evals.expected_output: Corrects both beliefs: explicit Protocol subclasses inherit default method bodies, and runtime isinstance on a runtime-checkable Protocol is about 5 to 9x a plain class check on 3.12+ (65 to 86x on 3.11), which only matters in a tight loop. Recommends a Protocol subclassed explicitly with @abstractmethod for members without a default, unless shared fields or nominal typing are needed.
expectations: Says explicit Protocol subclasses inherit default method bodies
Gives the isinstance cost as a version-dependent ratio (about 5 to 9x on 3.12+, much higher on 3.11), not a flat 100x
[auto] No ~100x or ~160x isinstance claim
[auto] Does not say Protocols cannot share code
[auto] Mentions @abstractmethod or a type checker

evals.prompt: Our FastAPI service loads a 2 GB model. What's the right pattern to make sure it's only loaded once? I was going to write a Singleton class.
evals.expected_output: No Singleton class: load it in the FastAPI lifespan and hand it to handlers, or use a module-level loader guarded by a lock. Notes that @cache or a PEP 562 module __getattr__ can run the loader more than once under concurrent first access.
expectations: Recommends loading in the lifespan (or composition root) and passing it in
Warns that @cache or module __getattr__ is not run-once under threads
[auto] No Singleton class
[auto] Mentions a lock or the lifespan
[auto] Mentions that @cache can run more than once under threads

evals.prompt: We're building an internal admin tool: a few forms over a Postgres table, maybe 20 users. I want to do it properly with CQRS and event sourcing from day one. Can you lay out the architecture?
evals.expected_output: Declines CQRS and Event Sourcing for a CRUD tool, citing the published warnings (Fowler: CQRS adds risky complexity for most systems; cosmicpython: a simple CRUD wrapper needs no domain model or repository), and gives the plain structure plus the seam that would allow event sourcing later if an audit trail appears.
expectations: Recommends against CQRS and Event Sourcing for this tool
